args.text: When labeling BPMN activities, preserve the action and direction of the interaction stated in the description; do not turn receiving feedback or evaluation into providing it, or otherwise change who performs or receives the action.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing documented guideline already covers faithful activity labels and preserving who does what.

result.rule: Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
For a message event, put messageRef on its bpmn:messageEventDefinition, never on the event element itself.
Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.

args.text: When labeling BPMN elements, use concise wording that preserves the meaning and direction of the described action, without adding unstated details or changing the actor, recipient, or outcome.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing learned guideline already covers semantic divergence in labels.

result.rule: When the description states an activity or outcome and identifies its action, object, actor, or recipient: label the corresponding BPMN element with concise wording that preserves those stated details and does not substitute a different action or meaning

When the description gives an activity with multiple evaluation dimensions or optional methods, or states a completion outcome in detail: Use concise labels for the corresponding BPMN activities and events, preserving the central action or outcome without enumerating subsidiary details.

When the description names a distinct activity or outcome and states its action or completion condition: Label the corresponding BPMN element with the described action or outcome. Do not replace it with a broader or narrower action, or add detail the description does not support.

When the description explicitly names multiple operations or specifies an activity’s object or recipient: Retain those stated details in the corresponding BPMN activity label so the label does not broaden or narrow the described work.
